name: Memphis, TN
subtitle: BBQ royalty, soul food, and the blues table
items: The Rendezvous (since 1948, dry-rubbed ribs in an alley — the original)
Gus's World Famous Fried Chicken (spicy, crispy, perfect)
Central BBQ (local chain done right — pulled pork & wings)
Cozy Corner (since 1977, BBQ Cornish hen — get it)
Payne's Bar-B-Q (Lamar Ave, chopped pork on a bun, legendary sauce)
Alcenia's (North Memphis, soul food, Betty Joyce Dean's cooking + hugs)
Restaurant Iris (Cooper-Young, Craig Blondis, New Orleans influence)
The Beauty Shop (Overton Square, Wally Joe — in a real converted salon)
Hog & Hominy (Overton Park, wood-fired Italian-Southern fusion)
Felicia Suzanne's (Downtown, fine Southern dining, catfish & crab)
Andrew Michael Italian Kitchen (East Memphis, two brothers, Zagat-lauded)
Flight Restaurant & Wine Bar (Downtown, share plates + 100 wines)
McEwen's on Monroe (Downtown, New American, excellent brunch)
Dyer's Burgers (Beale St, grease passed down since 1912 — you know the lore)
Soul Fish Café (Cooper-Young, catfish + shrimp po'boys)
Chez Philippe (Peabody Hotel, French fine dining — dress the part)
Alchemy (Cooper-Young, cocktail bar + elevated food)
Interim Restaurant (Cooper-Young, seasonal, estate farm)
Sweet Grass (Cooper-Young, coastal Southern)
The Arcade Restaurant (South Main, est. 1919 — Elvis' booth is still there)
